html:
The South Sudanese Civil War began on 15 December 2013, when fighting broke out in Juba between soldiers loyal to President Salva Kiir and those of his former vice president Riek Machar.

The split followed ethnic lines, with many Dinka behind Kiir and many Nuer behind Machar, and both sides massacred civilians. Towns such as Malakal and Bentiu changed hands several times. Famine was declared in parts of the country in 2017.

A study estimated about 400,000 deaths by 2018, and millions fled to Uganda and other neighbours. A peace deal in 2018 led to a unity government in February 2020, but violence and political crisis continued. It undid the hopes of independence in South Sudan, founded by the movement of John Garang.
sum: The South Sudanese Civil War began on 15 December 2013, when fighting broke out in Juba between soldiers loyal to President Salva Kiir and those of his former vice president Riek Machar.
